extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in politics and comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing a high-profile political roast/monologue (here, Michelle Wolf at the White House Correspondents' Dinner) with attention to target selection, tone, topicality, audience reaction, and appropriateness to the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target selection (public figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing who to roast or criticize — e.g., President Trump, Sarah Huckabee Sanders, Kellyanne Conway, Ivanka Trump, Mike Pence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece documents Wolf going after multiple Trump administration figures and notes specific jokes aimed at each (e.g., Sanders, Conway, Ivanka). Examples show that selecting prominent administration figures is central to this monologue's approach and shapes audience and media reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: raunchy versus nasty
rubrics_metrics.description: The balance of vulgarity/raunch and mean-spirited nastiness in the routine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Washington Post description that the routine “swerved from raunchy to downright nasty.” Use this criterion to evaluate whether the material is edgy but funny or crosses into gratuitous nastiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness to event/context
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the jokes suit the occasion (a journalists' dinner) and the expectations of that audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes 'This dinner is for journalists,' implying a boundary on targets/topics; consider whether the content respects or violates the event's norms and whether attacking a guest onstage (e.g., Sarah Huckabee Sanders sitting nearby) is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punching up vs punching down / presence of target
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the comedian is attacking powerful public figures (punching up) or making personal attacks that might be perceived as punching down, especially when the target is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The write-up highlights people wondering 'if she had gone too far' when Sanders was sitting nearby and absorbed criticism of her physical appearance and job performance. Use presence and relative power of target to judge ethical/critical reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topicality / use of current events
rubrics_metrics.description: How the routine incorporates recent news and hot-button issues (abortion, #MeToo, Trump administration scandals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The monologue references abortion, #MeToo, Trump skipping the dinner, and administration controversies. Evaluate how timely references add relevance or date the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic devices and craft (technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of specific comedic techniques such as insult/roast, simile/metaphor, juxtaposition, irony, wordplay, and callback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the article include lines like the 'smokey eye' metaphor for burning facts, joking similes (empty box of tampons), and insult structures. Assess clarity, wit, and originality of devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shock value and sexual/raunchy references
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of sexual imagery or shock lines (e.g., porn-star line about Trump) to provoke laughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece opens with a porn-star joke and includes sexual references to Trump's 'sexual prowess'; consider whether shock enhances the joke or alienates/overshadows the humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on appearance versus policy/performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether jokes attack a subject's physical appearance or address their job performance and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes criticism of Sanders' physical appearance along with her job performance; evaluators should weigh whether focusing on appearance is fair or gratuitous compared with critiquing professional actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reaction and critical reception
rubrics_metrics.description: How the audience and commentators responded (mixed reviews, outrage, praise, impressions of 'impressive' restraint by the target).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece reports 'mixed reviews in the room and online' and 'requisite outrage on the right (and some not so right).' Use audience and media reactions as a metric of success and controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of funny bits versus controversy overshadowing comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there are 'plenty of funny bits' that stand on their own, or whether controversy about specific lines dominates coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article states there were 'plenty of funny bits in between' despite controversy; evaluate if jokes hold up independently of the ensuing outrage.
